name: sgs/nav-menu
title: SGS Nav Menu
description: The site's primary navigation bar. A flat horizontal row of real links on desktop; below the collapse point it becomes a burger that opens the sgs/nav-drawer via the shared sgs/nav Interactivity store. Menu content comes from a native WordPress menu.

indicator.reason: style.css declares .sgs-nav-menu__indicator { pointer-events: none; } — the element is structurally unhoverable, the browser passes all pointer events through to whatever is underneath. It paints from the item Background row's own Hover swatch (itemBgHover / itemBgHoverGradient) under itemBgHoverTreatment === 'highlight' (Spec 41 FR-41-25), so its colour already carries that row's states rather than a parallel pair of its own.

submenu-bg.reason: The submenu panel's visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure toggled by the trigger, not by pointer position over the panel itself — once open, the pointer is always over some interactive CHILD, never a hoverable moment on the panel background itself. The hoverable surface inside the panel is the LINK background, which carries its own full three-state family (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent, Spec 41 FR-41-9) — that is where a hover fill belongs, and it is declared there.

submenu-border.reason: The panel's border sits on the same structurally non-hoverable surface as its background, for the same reason: once the panel is open the pointer is always over an interactive CHILD. Per-state border colour inside the panel belongs to the LINK, whose own three-state family (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent) is where a pointer-driven change is actually perceivable. submenuBorderColour is therefore Normal-only (Spec 41 FR-41-9).

wrapper.label: Nav wrapper
wrapper._note: The rendered <nav> (SGS_Container_Wrapper, composite-mirror rule R-31-9). Padding/margin ride the native spacing support; max-width is the flat attribute. navBg/navColour/navBgHover all write to the same bare $uid_sel wrapper selector (2026-08-28 fix — navBg previously only resolved via a hand-seeded attr-classification-overrides.json entry, not derivation; that override entry is now redundant, kept for now as a separate cleanup). The 12 ARRANGEMENT members (layer OUTER) — display/flex-direction/align-items/justify-content etc. — are honest GAPs: style.css:13-17 hardcodes `display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between` with no attribute behind any of it. Not fixed here — out of this task's scope (only STATE_WITHOUT_BASE cases are fixed).
wrapper._note_hover_nav: navColourHover declared 2026-09-05: render.php:872-873 emits sgs_hover_state_rules( "{$uid_sel}", 'color:…', ':focus-visible' ) — the block ROOT, so it belongs on the wrapper element, not a descendant.

bar.label: Item bar (flex row)
bar._note: The <ul class="sgs-nav-menu__bar"> that actually arranges the item links — distinct from `wrapper`, which arranges the bar against the burger toggle-wrap. Remaining ARRANGEMENT members are honest GAPs (style.css:19-26 hardcodes `display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap` with no attribute). `css:grid-template-columns:count` is a pseudo-property destination tag (mirrors `css:color-gradient` — not a real CSS property, a manifest-level routing key) claiming `listColumns` as this element's grid COLUMN-COUNT destination for the converter's grid resolver (`db.attr_for_grid_column_count`), matching render.php:1603-1624's own target selector `.sgs-nav-menu__bar` for the in-drawer vertical-list column count.

item.label: Nav item (resting)
item._note: The nav item LINK — every stateful control on this element targets the <a>, never the <li> (Spec 41 FR-41-1). Three states are declared: base, `hover` (render.php's `$hover_targets` = `:hover, :focus-visible`) and `current` (`[aria-current="page"]`), so a visitor can distinguish WHERE THEY ARE from WHAT THEY ARE POINTING AT. The current-page state is operator-controllable through `itemColourCurrent` / `itemBgCurrent` / `itemFontWeightCurrent` (Spec 41 FR-41-1); `itemFontWeightCurrent` is the non-colour signal that satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 without relying on colour alone. `current` deliberately maps DIFFERENT attribute names from `hover`: the classifier's `extract-signatures.py::_record` is last-write-wins, so a state map byte-identical to `hover` silently overwrites the hover derivation and tags those attributes with a css_state they never render in. Every state member is EXPLICIT rather than left to the `{prefix}Suffix` convention — `css:font-weight`, `css:text-decoration` and `css:text-transform` each carry a base attribute AND a state sibling, and without an explicit entry per state both derive to the same (property, element, state=NULL) slot and collide on one routing destination. The base `css:font-weight` -> `itemFontWeight` entry is load-bearing for the same reason: a state entry with no base is the STATE_WITHOUT_BASE shape the manifest gate flags. `css:border-radius` -> `itemBorderRadius` is base-only — radius has no state on `SgsBorderControl` (Spec 41 FR-41-7).

indicator.label: Sliding indicator
indicator._note: The `.sgs-nav-menu__indicator` sliding pill, view.js-animated behind the active/hovered item. It is rendered under `itemBgHoverTreatment === 'highlight'` and paints from the item Background row's OWN Hover swatch — `itemBgHover` / `itemBgHoverGradient`, claimed by the `item` element's `states.hover` (Spec 41 FR-41-25) — so this element routes no attribute of its own: one picker, one property, three ways of applying it. `clusters: ["fill"]` is retained (not `[]`) because the forward-resolution pass only visits a cluster's members when the cluster is declared; with an empty attrMap the fill members are honest GAPs, ungated and correct, since this element has no controls of its own. `supports.sgs.colourExemptions.indicator` records why it carries no hover state: style.css declares `.sgs-nav-menu__indicator { pointer-events: none; }`, so the element is structurally unhoverable.

featured.label: Featured item
featured._note: render.php:431-459. featuredFontWeightHover is a genuine hover-state weight change (only emitted when it differs from resting), declared under `text` cluster's css:font-weight member. featuredColourGradient added 2026-09-04 (mirrors burgerColourGradient's shape) -- explicit attrMap since css:color-gradient is not resolved by the default {prefix}Suffix convention, same reason burgerColourGradient needed one. Resting LABEL form only; PILL form and the submenu-inheritance custom property stay flat (see render.php comments). featuredBgGradient/featuredBgHoverGradient added 2026-09-06 (D958, Bean-directed preset-to-gradient upgrade) -- non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBg/featuredBgHover slug+hex; when active the pill foreground skips WCAG contrast-against-background maths (no single hex to test) and uses the operator's own flat colour instead (see render.php). The submenu-inheritance custom property stays hex-only, same scope boundary as featuredColourGradient above.

burger.label: Burger toggle
burger._note: burgerColour is the icon TEXT colour (css:color, render.php:466-469); burgerHoverColour drives the button's HOVER background-color (render.php:479-482, was 470-473 pre-fix), which previously had no resting counterpart — a client could style the hover fill but never the button's own resting fill (STATE_WITHOUT_BASE, Spec 35 FR-35-5). Fixed 2026-07-21 by adding the `burgerBg` base attribute + inspector control (edit.js Burger panel, Normal state) so css:background-color now resolves at base too. Unset burgerBg renders byte-identical to before (style.css:73-88 `background:none` default). 2026-09-05: `css:color`->burgerColour (render.php:1189-1196), `css:background-color`->burgerBg (render.php:1210-1213) and `states.hover.css:color`->burgerColourHover (render.php:1199-1201, sgs_hover_state_rules on `:hover, :focus-visible`) declared EXPLICITLY. Two DB-consistency findings drove this: (a) burgerColour + burgerColourHover both derived to (color, burger, state=NULL), colliding on one routing slot -- the hover entry is what separates them; (b) burgerBg carried a rogue `css_property='background-color'` seed present in NEITHER the derived classifier layer NOR the overrides, so it would have vanished on the next reseed. The manifest is the durable source; the stray seed is not removed here because the attribute genuinely paints that property.

sublink.label: Submenu link
sublink._note: The submenu LINK — <a class="sgs-nav-menu__sublink">, painted at render.php's own scoped `.sgs-nav-menu__sublink{...}` rule. It carries three states: base, `hover` (`sgs_hover_state_rules()` on `:hover, :focus-visible`) and `current` (`[aria-current="page"]`), matching the bar item's own three-state model (Spec 41 FR-41-1 / FR-41-9). `"prefix": ""` is a deliberate, permanent opt-out from the `{prefix}Suffix` convention: a `submenu` prefix would wrongly claim submenuAlign/Caret/CloseGrace/MinWidth/Padding and the whole submenuBorder* family, which belong to the submenu PANEL (the `submenu-panel` element) rather than to this anchor. The `submenu`-prefixed typography attributes that DO belong to this anchor reach it through the explicit attrMap entries above, one per property — that is the resolution, not a prefix (Spec 41 FR-41-22c). With an empty prefix nothing here resolves by convention, so every member is explicit by necessity: each state's `css:color`, `css:background-color`, `css:font-weight`, `css:text-decoration` and `css:text-transform` names a DIFFERENT attribute from its base sibling, because without an explicit entry a base and its state sibling both derive to (property, sublink, state=NULL) and collide on one routing slot. `"fill"` is declared alongside `"text"` so the forward-resolution pass actually visits css:background-color / css:background-image and consults this attrMap; a cluster that is not declared is never iterated. submenuColourGradient is routed as a DIRECT declaration (sgs_text_colour_decl / sgs_resolve_text_colour_or_gradient) rather than a colour-valued custom property, because a `var(--x, …)` chain feeding a fixed `color:` declaration cannot switch to `background-image` for a gradient (survey.js's `paints-via-colour-valued-custom-property` refusal reason).

submenu-panel.label: Submenu panel
submenu-panel._note: The floating dropdown PANEL — <div class="sgs-nav-menu__submenu"> — as distinct from the links inside it, which are the `sublink` element (Spec 41 FR-41-9). Base only: NO `states` key at all, because the panel has neither a hover nor a current state for any property. Its visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure toggled by the trigger; once open the pointer is always over an interactive CHILD, so a pointer-driven change on the panel surface itself is never perceivable — the hoverable surface inside the panel is the LINK background (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent on `sublink`). Recorded as `supports.sgs.colourExemptions.submenu-bg` and `.submenu-border`. `"prefix": ""` for the same reason `sublink` carries it: a `submenu` prefix would claim submenuColour* and the submenu typography family, which belong to the LINK. Every member is therefore explicit.

sgs._note_sweep_eligibility: The ONE declarative source for the Sweep-treatment eligibility predicate, read by BOTH surfaces — edit.js decides whether to offer the Sweep segment, render.php decides whether to emit Sweep CSS — with neither re-deriving the rule (Spec 41 FR-41-26). It is NOT an `elements` entry and routes no CSS property; it sits beside colourExemptions / hideExtensions / boxFamilies. Three keys per row: `blockingBackgroundAttrs` (Sweep is withdrawn when ANY named attribute is non-empty, because background-clip:text clips the element's whole background-painting area to the glyph shapes — every state's background counts, not just the resting one), `blockingGradientAttrs` (the row's own text gradient writes background-image on the identical selector, so whichever loses is invisible) and `glyphGuard` (background-clip:text needs glyphs to grip; null means the element always has them). Every attribute named below must exist in `attributes` — a typo reads as permanently empty, so the predicate would always pass and the rule would silently cease to exist.

attributes._note_nav_fill: Nav CONTAINER surface (2026-07-28). The block previously had NO fill controls at all — only per-ITEM colours — so a client could never sit the bar on its own surface. Scope is deliberately SURFACE ONLY: border/radius/divider were built and then REMOVED the same day (Bean ruling) because the pill-nav and bordered-nav patterns that justify them are whole-HEADER treatments, and sgs/site-header already declares `color` + `__experimentalBorder` supports for exactly that. Do not re-add them here without a header-level reason. Defaults unset, so an untouched nav renders byte-identically. Because the drawer holds its OWN sgs/nav-menu instance, these also give fully independent drawer styling with no extra plumbing.

navColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the nav text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour (D956 text-colour gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over navColour. Safe unconditionally -- navBg already paints on a separate ::after layer (sgs_block_background_layer_css()), never this same selector.

itemColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the resting nav-item text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour (D956 text-colour gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over itemColour. Safe unconditionally -- itemBg already paints on a ::before layer (D942 recipe item 1), never this same selector. Not offered on hover: itemColourHover's 'pill' style auto-computes its colour for WCAG contrast against itemBgHover.

itemBgGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the resting nav-item background via the same ::before layer as itemBg (D942 recipe item 1); non-empty wins over the flat itemBg colour, mirroring itemColourGradient's sibling-wins pattern.

featuredColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured bar item's LABEL-form text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour (mirrors burgerColourGradient). Non-empty wins over featuredColour. Resting LABEL form only (no featuredBg set) -- the PILL form (featuredBg set) keeps its WCAG-contrast-resolved flat foreground, and the submenu inheritance custom property (--sgs-nm-featured-colour) stays flat-only because its consumer paints a background on the same selector (see render.php).

featuredBgGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured item's PILL-form background (background-image custom-property-gradient pattern, D958 upgrade from slug-only). Non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBg slug/hex. When active, the pill's foreground SKIPS the WCAG contrast-against-background computation (sgs_wcag_preferred_text_colour_for_bg() needs ONE background hex; a gradient has none) and uses the operator's own FLAT featuredColour/featuredColourHover choice instead -- never the gradient-capable text resolve, which would collide with this same background-image on the same selector (see render.php comment at the featured-item paint block, and featuredColourGradient's note above for the identical precedent on the flat-hex pill form). The submenu-inherited featured item (--sgs-nm-featured-bg custom property) is NOT extended to carry this gradient -- same documented scope boundary as featuredColourGradient's submenu gap above.

featuredBgHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured item's PILL-form :hover/:focus-visible background (mirrors featuredBgGradient, D958). Non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBgHover slug/hex. Same WCAG-skip rationale as featuredBgGradient: the hover foreground uses the operator's own flat featuredColourHover (falling back to featuredColour) rather than computing WCAG contrast against a gradient.

attributes._note_three_state_model: Spec 41: every stateful control on this block targets the LINK, in three states — Normal, Hover (:hover, :focus-visible) and Current ([aria-current="page"]). The nav BAR keeps two states (navBg/navColour + their Hover siblings): a bar is never 'the current page'. The submenu PANEL keeps one (FR-41-9): its visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure, so the hoverable surface inside it is the LINK, which carries the full three-state family. Every new small string attribute below is declared WITHOUT a JSON enum and is validated in PHP instead: an out-of-enum stored value is silently coerced back to the block.json default with no error, which bites hardest via a programmatic writer (the cloning converter, a theme pattern) setting the attribute directly. The one exception is the pre-existing itemTextDecoration, which carries a real enum and keeps it — a disclosed asymmetry with its own hover sibling, not an oversight.

itemBgCurrentGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the current-page nav item's background via the same ::before layer as itemBg; non-empty wins over the flat itemBgCurrent colour.

itemBgHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the hovered nav item's background via the same ::before layer as itemBg; non-empty wins over the flat itemBgHover colour. It completes the row's three-state gradient set (itemBgGradient / this / itemBgCurrentGradient) and is what the Highlight treatment paints with when the operator picks a gradient (Spec 41 FR-41-25).

itemFontWeightCurrent.description: The non-colour current-page signal (Spec 41 FR-41-6), so the state is distinguishable without relying on colour alone. String, not number — matches itemFontWeight.

itemFontWeightHover.description: String, not number — matches itemFontWeight and itemFontWeightCurrent. A weight change on hover can reflow the bar; the control's help text carries that caution.

itemSmartContrast.description: Resolves the item's foreground automatically so it stays readable against whatever background the item is sitting on (Spec 41 FR-41-5).

itemBorderRadius.description: A FLAT corner object of CSS length STRINGS, read by sgs_corner_object_shorthand(), which looks for exactly topLeft / topRight / bottomRight / bottomLeft. NOT the {"desktop":{}} tier envelope — that shape belongs to BLOCK-ROOT radii read by sgs_border_radius_tiers(); used here it would carry no corner keys, the helper would return null, and the radius would silently vanish. Per-element precedent: sgs/product-card::ctaBorderRadius.

itemColourHoverTreatment.description: How the item TEXT colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. The Sweep option is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.itemColourHoverTreatment passes (Spec 41 FR-41-26). PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemBgHoverTreatment.description: How the item BACKGROUND changes on hover: none / swap / highlight. 'highlight' renders the sliding pill, painting from itemBgHover / itemBgHoverGradient (Spec 41 FR-41-25). PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemBorderHoverTreatment.description: How the item BORDER colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

borderHoverAnimationDirection.description: Secondary control, shown only when itemBorderHoverTreatment is 'sweep'. left-to-right / right-to-left. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuLinkBgGradient.description: Normal-state gradient sibling of submenuLinkBg; non-empty wins over the flat colour.

submenuColourHoverTreatment.description: How the submenu LINK text colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.submenuColourHoverTreatment passes. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuLinkBgHoverTreatment.description: How the submenu LINK background changes on hover: none / swap. Two options only — there is no Highlight on this row. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuAnimation.description: The submenu panel's open animation. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuBorderRadius.description: The submenu panel's corner radius — the same FLAT corner object shape as itemBorderRadius (topLeft / topRight / bottomRight / bottomLeft, CSS length strings, read by sgs_corner_object_shorthand()). Its default stays EMPTY: the panel already renders its own radius from --sgs-nm-submenu-radius with a token fallback, so there is no behaviour here for a default to preserve.

submenuBorderColourGradient.description: Normal-state gradient sibling of submenuBorderColour; non-empty wins over the flat colour.

submenuShadowColour.description: The shadow's colour. The name is fixed by ShadowControl.js::shadowAttrKeys, which composes it as <base>Colour.

submenuFontSize.description: A {desktop,tablet,mobile} TIER OBJECT, mirroring itemFontSize. There are deliberately no submenuFontSizeTablet / submenuFontSizeMobile siblings: TypographyControls and sgs_typography_css_rule() both branch on whether the stored value is an object and keep all three tiers inside this one attribute, so flat tier keys would have zero writers and zero readers.

sublinkMarkerColour.description: Normal-only, with no Hover or Current sibling. The marker is aria-hidden decoration beside the sublink's own text; unset, it inherits currentColor from that text, which already carries the full three-state colour, so it changes with Hover and Current for free.

triggerMode.description: What the menu button shows: icon / text / icon-and-text. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

triggerMagnetRadius.description: Pull radius in pixels, 20-400 — the range matches fx-magnet.js's own clamp.

triggerMagnetStrength.description: Pull strength, 2-80 — the range matches fx-magnet.js's own clamp.

burgerColourHoverTreatment.description: How the menu button's ICON/TEXT colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.burgerColourHoverTreatment passes. Governs burgerColour / burgerColourHover (the icon colour), NOT burgerHoverColour (the button's hover BACKGROUND) — the two names are anagram-close and govern different properties. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

burgerBgHoverTreatment.description: How the menu button's BACKGROUND changes on hover: none / swap. Two options only. Governs burgerBg / burgerHoverColour. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.
